transcript: Having now been to the show twice, I want to talk a little bit about my experiences with the cabaret pre show as well. Some tips and tricks for anyone going in the future. Tours for the pre show open about an hour before your show starts, and I definitely recommend getting there as early as possible. I think more people are catching on to this because the first time I went there really wasn't much of a line. We basically walked right in. However, going back this past week, there was actually a decent line to get in, although it did move very quickly. However, once inside, I felt like they did a really good job with crowd management and I never really felt too crowded. The experience is divided into three different floors. You come in on the Red Level and then you can go down to the gold level or up to the Green Level. Gold level is where the most things happen, so if you're looking for one spot to just park the entire time, this is definitely the spot to do it. There is a stage setup that pretty much has constant performances going on on it, as well as a bar if you wanna buy a drink. There's actually a bar on every single level, and the bar on the Red Level even sells some food in the theater itself. There are also QR codes on each of the arms of the seats that you can scan And order food to your seats. It's all pre prepared food so it's very quick. So if you're someone who wants some food or drink but don't wanna wait in line or deal with crowds, this is a good option. However, in terms of the pre show, there really isn't anything going on inside the theater itself. One of the mistakes I made my first time was we got seated early expecting something to be happening inside the theater, and we just kind of sat in an empty theater for 15 minutes. So I recommend staying in the pre show as long as you can until they tell you it's time to be seated. In terms of my recommended route, I would say start in the gold level before it gets too crowded right at the very beginning, and then as it starts to fill up, go and explore the rest of the. If you go up to the Red Level, they do have a small performance space in the back of the bar. This is a great spot to watch some of the performers up close without dealing with the large crowd in the Gold Room. And then definitely be sure to check out the green bar. Although in my experience there isn't a ton of performance that happens here, so you don't have to spend a ton of time. Be sure to make your way back down to the Gold Room for the final sequence. It involves pretty much All of the performers coming together for one last sequence, and it's really fun. And then once that's over, they'll usher everyone up to their seats to give you a sense of time. I believe the pre show ended about 10 of, after which all of the pre show performers go into the main theater where they play until the show starts.
